analysis.title: Has The AI Selloff Gone Too Far, Or Is Wall Street Front-Running Estimate Cuts?
key_insights: Goldman's Lee Coppersmith says client sentiment on AI is about as negative as it has been in quite some time, and the pessimism now shows in positioning and valuations. Article is dated Nov 16, 2026.
Goldman prime book data shows Tech was the most net sold sector globally again last week. The US Info Tech long/short ratio fell to its lowest in the dataset going back to 2016.

Flows have changed in kind. Earlier weeks were mainly long liquidation and de-grossing, and last week saw a more pronounced pickup in new shorts. Goldman's cash desk also saw persistent NVDA supply from long-only clients, with money rotating into hyperscalers and other large cap tech.
Hedge funds are more than 20 points underweight tech versus the S&P, and the tech long/short ratio fell from above 2 in the summer to roughly 1.5.

CTA positioning in NDX is back near max short levels. Coppersmith says that with positioning this light, it probably doesn't take much positive news to spark a squeeze higher. The SOX rose almost 7% last Monday as shorts covered.

Semis have underperformed the S&P by more than 30 percentage points since June, the sharpest relative drawdown since 2002. The SOX/SPX ratio was 31.5% below its trailing one-year high on Friday, against a record of -57.3% in November 2000.

The GS AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P, while consensus expects 31% earnings growth in 2028. At the S&P multiple, current prices would imply earnings falling about 6%. Either the selloff went too far or investors are pricing estimate cuts.
The article argues that when the sell side and the market disagree this much, estimates tend to follow price, though price targets also tend to follow price.

Clients' two main concerns are who pays for hundreds of billions of dollars of added AI spending, and whether enough data centers can be built. Goldman thinks the second is overdone. Even in a bearish scenario, 2028 new data center capacity should be roughly in line with 2027, and could be more than 50% higher if more projects proceed.

About 37GW of capacity is already under construction for 2028, roughly matching 2027. The upside depends on announced projects not yet started. Bernstein's audit found only about a quarter of announced US data center capacity is credible, and the article cites Texas siting restrictions and a derailed $5 billion Maryland campus as political risks.

Coppersmith calls financing the bigger worry. AI companies want to spend more than the cash they generate, borrowing costs are rising, and GIR thinks existing NVDA commitments should hold but new deals of the same size may be harder to arrange.

AI-related IG spreads are at roughly 140bps, the wides of the past two years and about 40bps over non-AI credit. Goldman expects 2027 US credit issuance above $2.7 trillion, with $4.1 trillion of off-balance sheet obligations still to be funded.

NVDA reports Tuesday after the close, its first print since its founder's exit, with the stock down 30% and down six weeks in a row. Anthropic is set to start trading two days later after an order book reportedly several times oversubscribed.

Goldman's 2027 Markets Outlook says AI spending should keep growing but the pace could peak early next year. AI accounted for 21% of US GDP growth, 62% of earnings growth and at the peak 92% of the S&P's gain in market value, so a slowdown matters more for stocks than for GDP.

Coppersmith's stance: equities can grind higher after the positioning reset, but be more selective. Use weakness to add rather than chase rallies, expect rotation beyond infrastructure, and stay disciplined on hedges. The article adds that Goldman's macro desk is calling for a squeeze into year-end, and that it expects the credit market, not the prime book, to answer who pays.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman Research argues the semis selloff has partly gone too far on valuation and positioning. Coppersmith prefers selectivity, adding on weakness and keeping hedges because AI spending growth may peak and financing is getting more expensive.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports Tuesday after the close, its first print since its founder's exit. The stock is down 30% over six consecutive weekly declines.

GS AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P. Consensus estimate (not a reported figure) is for 31% basket earnings growth in 2028, and at the S&P multiple prices would imply roughly a 6% decline.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman expects another record year of US credit issuance on top of near-record equity supply, adding to the funding burden for AI spending.

trade_ideas.description: Add selectively to AI-related equity exposure on weakness rather than chase rallies, while keeping hedges in place
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning has reset and parts of AI look interesting again, but spending growth is peaking and financing is more expensive.
trade_ideas.risk: A weak Anthropic debut or NVDA print, or estimate cuts that validate the market's implied earnings decline.

risk_factors: Financing: AI companies spend more than the cash they generate, borrowing costs are rising and AI-related IG spreads are at the wides.
Junk buyers have left the market and $4.1 trillion of off-balance sheet obligations remain to be funded.
AI spending growth could peak early next year, which matters more for stocks than for GDP given AI's share of earnings growth.
Data center buildout upside depends on announced projects, only about a quarter of which Bernstein finds credible, and on local politics.
A weak Anthropic IPO debut could weigh on the whole AI trade, per a Thiel lieutenant cited in the article.
Estimates may follow prices lower, validating the earnings decline the market is pricing for AI semis.

tension_points.bull_case: The GS AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P despite consensus 2028 growth of 31%, and hedge funds, long-onlies and CTAs are already out or short, so a squeeze is possible.
tension_points.bear_case: Estimates tend to follow price when the sell side and market disagree this much, so the market may be front-running cuts to earnings forecasts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cuts to 2028 earnings estimates that confirm the roughly 6% decline implied by prices, or a weak Anthropic debut, which the article says one Thiel lieutenant warned could pop the whole AI trade.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman thinks existing NVDA commitments should hold, and about 37GW under construction for 2028 roughly matches 2027, so the buildout continues even in a bearish scenario.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-related IG spreads are around 140bps and 40bps wider than non-AI credit, junk buyers are gone, and new deals of the same size may be harder to arrange while issuance reaches a record.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI spending growth peaking early next year, per Goldman's 2027 Markets Outlook, while financing costs keep rising.
